Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at MedBridge liked the latency profile and the observability hooks. We want to run a larger pilot in Q4 (30M tokens/month, multi-team) but our procurement team needs a commercial guardrail: a lower unit price for the pilot period and a commitment to a tiered pricing path if we convert.

We understand this is above standard discounts; we wanted to see if Redwood can treat this as a strategic proof-of-value given the potential volume and our enterprise references.

Can you route this to pricing/ops for an exception memo? Procurement is on a tight timeline.

Lauren — attaching a short exception memo (discount_exception_memo_grace_v1.pdf) and the model Grace shared. Summary below; asking for your signoff or guidance on limits.

Deal: MedBridge Health (HB-2027-0792) — Pilot: 12 weeks, estimated consumption 30M tokens/month. Prospect wants a 45% effective discount for the pilot and an option to convert to a 12-month committed capacity agreement with predictable step-down pricing.

Why we recommend making an exception:
- Strategic reference in the health vertical; strong case studies and PR potential.
- Likelihood of conversion: sales expects 60-70% probability within 6 months post-pilot if SLAs hold.
- Technical fit: low per-token compute due to caching and batching; modeled incremental cost is ~35% of list at peak.

Proposed concession (conservative):
- Approve a 40% effective discount for the pilot (vs 45% ask), conditional on:
  - Minimum conversion commit: 12 months at 60% of pilot volume (or financial penalty equivalent)
  - Usage floor for the pilot month 2–3 combined (to protect runway)
  - 30-day rev rec review and monthly usage reporting to Sales Ops

Financial impact: modeled lost margin vs standard pricing is acceptable if conversion happens; downside risk capped by minimum commit and short pilot window. See spreadsheet tab "Scenario A/B/C."

Attachments: discount_exception_memo_grace_v1.pdf (exec summary + financials), pricing_model_q4_pilot.xlsx (detailed model).

Request: please sign or provide a redline to the memo. If you approve, we'll issue a pilot amendment and short-side term sheet for MedBridge procurement.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
